mainTopic: רבא's two contradictions: whether color (חזותא) counts as a real substance, and whether non-food growth like wood has קדושת שביעית.
overview: The גמרא brings two contradictions raised by רבא. First, a משנה about ערלה says a garment dyed with ערלה peels must be burned, which shows that color (חזותא) counts as a real substance. But a משנה about corpse blood counts blood in a garment only if a רביעית washes out, so the stain itself seems to count for nothing. רב כהנא answers that the blood case is a special leniency, because דם תבוסה is impure only מדרבנן. Second, a משנה gives dye plants קדושת שביעית, which suggests even inedible growth like wood has the sanctity. A ברייתא says leaves gathered for fuel have none. רבא answers from the word 'לאכלה': the sanctity applies only to things whose benefit comes while they are used up, which excludes wood burned for its coals. The גמרא objects that wood burned for warmth does give benefit while it burns, and רבא's reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא's first source: a garment dyed with ערלה peels must be burned
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה that a garment dyed with ערלה peels must be burned, and infers that appearance (color) counts as a real substance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא pointed out a contradiction. We learned in a משנה: a garment dyed with ערלה peels must be burned. This shows that appearance (color) is a real thing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a contradiction by quoting the first of two sources. This step sets up the clash that comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the dye has soaked into the garment, only the color is left, not the peels themselves. Yet the משנה still forbids the garment as ערלה. So רבא concludes that color alone is treated as a real presence of the forbidden thing.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction (between two sources)
We learned (in a משנה)
Fruit of a tree in its first three years, forbidden for any benefit
Apparently / this shows that
Appearance is a real thing (it counts halachically)

phrases.english: Rava raised a contradiction: we learned:
A garment that one dyed with peels of orla must be burned;
apparently, appearance is a significant matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new contradiction raised by רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A garment dyed with ערלה peels must be burned, which shows that color (חזותא) counts as a real substance.

steps.title: The contradicting משנה begins: blood absorbed in a house
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a second משנה about a רביעית of corpse blood absorbed into a house, with two opinions that are reconciled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he contrasted it with another source: a רביעית of blood that was absorbed into a house — the house is impure. And some say: the house is pure. They do not really disagree: one is talking about vessels that were there from the start, and the other about vessels that came in later.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins quoting the contradicting משנה. This part is background; the real clash comes in the next line about a garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two opinions about the house look opposite, but the גמרא explains they are about different vessels. Vessels already in the house when the blood was absorbed become impure, while vessels brought in after the blood soaked in stay pure.

keyTerms.meaning: And raise a contradiction (from this source)
A quarter-log of blood, the amount of corpse blood that makes things impure in a tent
And some say it (another version)
And they do not disagree

phrases.english: And raise a contradiction: a quarter-log of blood that was absorbed in a house —
phrases.notes: This is blood from a dead person, which makes things under the same roof impure.

phrases.english: the house is impure.
And some say: the house is pure.
And they do not disagree,
this one is about vessels that were there from the outset,
that one is about vessels that came at the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the second source that will contradict step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from step 1 that appearance counts as a real substance.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up a משנה about absorbed blood whose next clause will treat absorbed color as not counting.

steps.title: Blood absorbed in a garment only counts if it can be washed out
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: blood in a garment is impure only if a רביעית comes out when washed, so blood that only colors the garment seems not to count.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the blood was absorbed in a garment, we check: if the garment is washed and a רביעית of blood comes out of it, it is impure; and if not, it is pure!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual clash. Here the משנה ignores blood that stays in the garment as mere color, which goes against רבא's conclusion from the ערלה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only blood that can actually be washed out is counted toward the רביעית. The blood that stays in as a stain is treated as nothing, which suggests that appearance (חזותא) is not a real substance. That directly contradicts the ערלה dye ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Was absorbed / soaked in
A garment / clothing
We examine / check
Is washed (laundered)

phrases.english: If it was absorbed in a garment — we examine it;
if the garment is washed
and a quarter-log of blood comes out of it — it is impure,
and if not — it is pure!
phrases.notes: So the blood left behind as a stain doesn't count — just color, which clashes with the ערלה ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradicting משנה and delivers the clash with step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's inference that חזותא מילתא היא (step 1).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If blood that only stains a garment is ignored, then mere color is not a real substance, contradicting the ruling that a ערלה-dyed garment is forbidden.

steps.title: רב כהנא: the blood case is a special rabbinic leniency
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that the garment ruling is one of the leniencies of רביעית, since it deals with דם תבוסה, which is only impure מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: this is taught here as one of the leniencies of רביעית measurements; it is about דם תבוסה, which is impure only by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא resolves the contradiction by saying the garment case is a special leniency. So in general, color still counts as a real thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דם תבוסה is the mixed blood that flows from a person around the time of death, and its impurity is only מדרבנן. Because the רבנן made this impurity, they could be lenient and count only blood that washes out. This does not change the general rule that appearance is significant, as in the ערלה case.

keyTerms.meaning: From the leniencies of quarter-log measurements
They taught here
Blood of submission — mixed blood flowing from a person at death
By rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: The general rule stays: color (חזותא) counts as a real substance. The garment-blood case is only an exception, because דם תבוסה is a rabbinic impurity and the רבנן were lenient with it.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
They taught here from among the leniencies of quarter-logs;
it is about blood of submission, which is impure by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: מִקּוּלֵּי רְבִיעִיּוֹת שָׁנוּ כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 2-3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the contradicting source to a special case (rabbinic leniency).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The garment-blood ruling seemed to show that color never counts as a real substance.
steps.terutzMaskana: The garment-blood ruling is an exception for דם תבוסה, a rabbinic impurity; in general חזותא מילתא היא.

steps.title: רבא's second contradiction: dye plants have שביעית sanctity
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה that wild-growing dye plants have שביעית sanctity and ביעור, and infers that even wood (inedible growth) has קדושת שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised another contradiction. We learned in a משנה: among the dye species, ספיחים of woad and safflower have שביעית sanctity, and so does the money exchanged for them; they must be removed (ביעור), and so must the money exchanged for them. This shows that wood has קדושת שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new contradiction by quoting the first source. This step sets up the clash, and the contradicting source comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Woad and safflower are not food; people use them for dye. Even so, the משנה gives them the full laws of שביעית, including for money exchanged for them and ביעור. So רבא concludes that even inedible growth like wood can have קדושת שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: From the species used for dyeing
Plants that grew by themselves, without being planted
Woad and safflower (dye plants)
Removing שביעית produce from one's home once it is gone from the fields
The holiness of produce of the seventh (Sabbatical) year

phrases.english: Rava raised a contradiction: we learned:
From among the species used for dyeing —
the self-grown plants of woad and safflower,
they have Sabbatical sanctity and their money has Sabbatical sanctity,
phrases.notes: "Their money" means money received in exchange for these plants.

phrases.english: they are subject to eradication and their money is subject to eradication.
Apparently, wood has in it
the sanctity of the Sabbatical Year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the first contradiction, the גמרא brings a second, separate contradiction from רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dye plants that grew by themselves in שביעית have קדושת שביעית and ביעור, which shows that even inedible wood has קדושת שביעית.

steps.title: A ברייתא says leaves gathered for fuel have no שביעית sanctity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא contrasts רבא's inference with a ברייתא. Reed and vine leaves gathered for eating have קדושת שביעית, but leaves gathered for wood do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A contradiction was raised: reed leaves and vine leaves that someone piled up for storage on the field have קדושת שביעית if he gathered them to eat. If he gathered them for wood, they do not have קדושת שביעית!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his own contradiction. He sets a ברייתא that says the opposite against the inference from step 5 that wood has קדושת שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 suggested that even things that are not food, like wood, have שביעית sanctity. Here the very same leaves have sanctity when meant for food but none when meant for fuel. So wood used as wood seems to have no קדושת שביעית, which clashes with step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction: one source is set against another
The holiness of produce that grew in the seventh year
He piled them up or gathered them into a heap
For use as wood or fuel

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: This sets the ברייתא coming up against what רבא just said in step 5.

phrases.english: Reed leaves and vine leaves
that one piled up for storage on the field,
if he gathered them for eating,
they are subject to the sanctity of the seventh year;
if he gathered them for wood,
they are not subject to the sanctity of the seventh year!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the inference in step 5 that wood has קדושת שביעית.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's inference that even wood has קדושת שביעית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says leaves meant for fuel have no קדושת שביעית, so wood used as fuel should not have it either.

steps.title: The פסוק 'for food' limits שביעית to benefit that comes while the item is used up
steps.stepSummary: Based on 'לאכלה', קדושת שביעית applies only to things whose benefit and use-up happen together. Wood is excluded because its benefit comes after it burns.
steps.simpleTranslation: The answer: the פסוק says 'for food'. This means the sanctity applies to something whose benefit comes at the same time it is used up, like food. Wood is left out, since you benefit from it only after it is used up.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own contradiction with a rule taken from the פסוק. The ברייתא's leaves-for-fuel are excluded because of how fuel gives its benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food is enjoyed in the very act of eating it, and dye plants likewise give their benefit, the color, as they are used up in dyeing. That is why the dye plants in step 5 have the sanctity. Burning wood mostly gives its benefit afterward, through the coals that heat the oven, so the fuel leaves in step 6 fall outside קדושת שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: And he answers or reconciles the contradiction
'For food' (ויקרא 25:6), the source for this rule
Benefit or enjoyment
Here: the item being used up or consumed

steps.confusionAlert: Here ביעור means the item being used up. It is not the ביעור from step 5, which means removing seventh-year produce from your house.
steps.whyThisMatters: This 'benefit and use-up at the same time' rule is the test that decides which non-food items carry קדושת שביעית.

phrases.english: And he answers:
The verse states: "for food"
meaning something whose benefit and whose being used up happen together,
which excludes wood,
whose benefit comes after it is used up.
phrases.notes: With a fire, you mainly benefit from the hot coals left after the wood burns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from the ברייתא in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on a פסוק: different kinds of use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed wood either always has קדושת שביעית (step 5) or never has it (step 6).
steps.terutzMaskana: Only things whose benefit and use-up happen together have the sanctity. Dye plants qualify, so the משנה stands. Wood used for fuel does not qualify, so the ברייתא stands.

steps.title: But wood burned for warmth gives benefit while it burns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that wood used for warming does give benefit at the same time it is used up, so it should fit the rule and have קדושת שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is wood used for warmth, where the benefit and the burning happen at the same time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 7. Some wood gives its benefit right while it burns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said wood is excluded because its benefit comes afterward. But when you warm yourself by a fire, you enjoy the heat while the wood is burning. So that kind of wood should meet the 'same time' test, and the ברייתא's ruling that fuel has no sanctity still needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't there? An opener for an objection
Used for warming oneself

phrases.english: But isn't there wood used for warmth,
whose benefit and being used up happen together!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that wood's benefit always comes after it is used up
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wood burned for warmth gives benefit while it burns, so it should have קדושת שביעית, and the ברייתא's ruling on leaves for fuel is again hard to explain.

steps.title: רבא begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts to answer the objection about wood used for warmth. His actual answer comes on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup: the גמרא is introducing רבא's reply to the objection about wood used for warmth. The content of his answer comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is stated yet. The learner should expect רבא to explain why the ברייתא still says wood used as fuel has no קדושת שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא said, introducing his response

phrases.english: Rava said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the response to the objection in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pending: the answer continues on the next amud
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wood used for warmth seems to meet the 'same time' rule.
